subject: Operational advisory: targeted connectivity disruption — endpoint migration plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Operational advisory: targeted connectivity disruption — endpoint migration plan

Hi Sara,

Quick heads-up: starting ~09:05 UTC we observed elevated request error rates and latency spikes for requests routed to our EU edge (eu-west-2) and several APAC PoPs. Our network team has traced this to an upstream peering control-plane partition at one of the public cloud providers (vendor ticket in cc). Impact: a subset of requests to eu-* and apac-* endpoints are returning 502/504 or timing out; overall system is still healthy if traffic is routed via our US endpoints.

Immediate recommendation for customers affected (short-term mitigations):
- Switch inference traffic from your regional endpoints to the us-west-1 cluster (no model change required) by updating your API host to: api.us-west-1.redwood.ai (or use the regional alias we provide).
- TTLs: lower your DNS TTL to 60s if you can, to speed cutover.
- We have attached a short playbook (endpoint-migration-playbook.pdf) and an edge topology map (edge_map_v2.png).

We can coordinate a guided migration window if you want us to execute the DNS alias on our side. Proposed window: 14:30–15:00 PST today (Nov 20). The process should be non-destructive; expect a brief burst of increased latency for a handful of calls during the cutover (~30–60s).

Please reply with either:
1) "We opt-in" and a preferred window, or
2) "We cannot move now" and details on constraints so we can propose alternate mitigations.

We understand this is disruptive—our CS and engineering teams will be on the call and available to help.

Attachments: endpoint-migration-playbook.pdf (step-by-step), edge_map_v2.png

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Manager\Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-ml.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Theo Mendes <theo@eurocloudops.io>, support@peervendor.net
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational advisory: targeted connectivity disruption — endpoint migration plan

Jordan —

Thanks for the alert. We've been seeing intermittent 500s in our production cascade starting ~09:00 UTC and a small uptick in tail latency. We are onboard to migrate to us-west-1 but need to confirm a couple things:
- Will session-affinity or any sticky routing be affected? We rely on short-lived session affinity for streaming sessions.
- Any expected impact to token billing or concurrency limits during the cutover?

Also, do you anticipate this lasting beyond today? If it's likely to be multi-day we'll need to involve our platform team to schedule a more controlled migration.

Quick ask: can Redwood confirm whether you'll proactively manage the DNS alias change or whether we should update our in-app endpoint override?

— Sara Lim
Head of ML Platform, Acme ML

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Operational advisory: targeted connectivity disruption — endpoint migration plan

Jordan / team — quick internal note (not to customer):

We confirmed with vendor (support@peervendor.net) that a control-plane partition impacted BGP session resets across three peering routers in eu-west-2; APAC PoPs that depend on those peers experienced indirect route flaps. Mitigation we can do now:
- Activate DNS alias to point acme-specific alias -> api.us-west-1.redwood.ai and reduce TTL to 60s.
- Enable short-lived affinity fallback: service will preserve streaming sessions by using connection-level keepalive and will re-establish on new host; sticky tokens are stored in the client; we will not invalidate session tokens.
- No model version/parameter changes required. Concurrency limits: temporary burst will be counted against us-west-1 quotas; we have capacity headroom but will throttle at 95% of committed throughput and will alert you.

I'll prepare a short migration checklist and coordinate the live window. If Acme opts in we can run the cutover in ~3h.

— Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Theo Mendes <theo@eurocloudops.io>, support@peervendor.net
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational advisory: targeted connectivity disruption — endpoint migration plan

Sara — thanks for the quick reply and the questions. Short answers up front: session affinity will be preserved by client re-attach (no token invalidation), and we do not expect any permanent billing delta beyond transient egress differences; we will credit any measurable impact per our SLA (we'll follow up separately on credits).

Planned migration (per Acme opt-in):
- Window: 14:30–14:50 PST today (Nov 20).
- Action: Redwood will flip the DNS alias for acme-prod.redwood.ai -> api.us-west-1.redwood.ai and lower authoritative TTL to 60s; we will announce the change on the Slack incident channel and monitor for 30 minutes after.
- Expected behaviour: most traffic will failover cleanly; streaming clients will reconnect and resume within ~30–60s. Some clients with aggressive DNS caching may need manual override.
- Rollback: If error rate increases >5% over baseline for >5 minutes we will roll back immediately to previous routing and open a bridge with Acme.

Attachments: endpoint-migration-playbook.pdf (detailed step list). Please confirm "We opt-in" to this window and we'll proceed to execute from our side. If you prefer to flip from your side, reply with the time you'll make the change and we will stand by.

Best,
Jordan
Senior Account Manager\Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Theo Mendes <theo@eurocloudops.io>, support@peervendor.net
Date: Thu, 23 Nov 2028 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — 2028-11-20 regional peering partition

Sara / Acme team —

Follow-up and brief postmortem for the disruption on Nov 20 that affected EU/APAC egress to our inference edge. Summary highlights:
- Root cause: upstream peering control-plane partition at Peervendor that caused BGP session resets in eu-west-2, which cascaded to several APAC PoPs dependent on those routes. (Vendor ticket: PV-128334).
- What we did: coordinated with Peervendor, activated our us-west-1 alias for impacted customers, executed DNS migration for Acme at 14:30 PST, monitored traffic and rolling metrics.
- Impact: 7–12% request error rate for affected EU/APAC requests during the incident window; Acme observed intermittent 500s and tail latency increases. No model data loss; all customer data was handled per normal retention.
- Remediation & follow-ups:
  1) Redwood will pursue a permanent multi-homing adjustment for EU PoPs to remove single-peer dependency (timeline: 4–6 weeks).
  2) We will add an automated customer-facing reroute toggle in the console (ETA: 3 weeks).
  3) Offer: Redwood will issue a one-time credit equivalent to 10% of the billed inference spend for Nov 20 for customers demonstrably impacted; Monica will follow up with Acme on credit calculation and HubSpot record.

Attachments: postmortem-digest.txt (non-sensitive summary), endpoint-migration-playbook.pdf (for reference).

We appreciate your patience. If you want a deeper technical readout or a short postmortem bridge with our infra leads and Peervendor, we can schedule that this week.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Manager\Redwood Inference
Attachments: postmortem-digest.txt, endpoint-migration-playbook.pdf
